cards.title: Simulation Strategies for Exposure Prediction
cards.claim: Simulations can predict exposures for untested regimens or populations. Strategies include: (1) Fixed-effect estimates for typical profiles; (2) Uncertainty in fixed effects to assess probability of exposure cutoffs; (3) Between-subject variability (BSV) and residual error to show individual concentration ranges. Correlations between random effects must be accounted for to avoid unrealistic parameter combinations.
conditions: Models must be revalidated if the simulation purpose differs from the original model purpose.
Simulations for future populations must account for uncertainty in BSV and fixed effects.
Demographic variables for simulation should reflect the target population.
limitations: Predictions based on typical parameters are not mean predictions.
Uncertainty increases when simulating beyond clinically studied scenarios.
Shrinkage limits reliability of individual predictions if not accounted for.
cards.downstream_use: Prospective human PK prediction; dose regimen selection; exposure-response analysis.

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
